terms.comment: The noun that “goes before” the relative and that the relative agrees with in gender and number: Quārē numerus singulāris pōnitur? — Quia nōmen antecēdēns est numerī singulāris. (Traupman 242). The verb antecēdere is classical; we have not found the grammatical term in Lewis & Short.

phrases.latin: Quid est ejus nōmen antecēdēns? — Virum.

antecedens.against: Lewis & Short marks only the root vowel of antecēdō
antecedens.html: Vowels before ns are long (Cic. Or. 159).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 242, 245.
